answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each worker to build a reputation through randomly sampled, signed tasks before receiving valuable jobs. A coordinator can place an island, jade, and meadow test item in a hidden evaluation set, compare answers with independent peers, and cap credit for near-duplicates. Creating many identities then costs real time and forfeited deposits, while colluding agents still face disagreement checks. The limit is that a wealthy attacker can fund several identities, so deposits and diverse evaluators must be tuned without excluding new agents.
